rationale: zone.js replaces the global Promise with ZoneAwarePromise (promise.ts:585, `global['Promise'] = ZoneAwarePromise`). zone.js's own Promise.spec.ts has a 'Promise.any' suite that takes `(Promise as any).any` into a local alias and calls it repeatedly (lines 664+). That is a real in-repo test caller reaching ZoneAwarePromise.any through the global monkey-patch plus a local alias. No in-scope rule covers callers that reach a method through runtime replacement of a global binding. If the spec file is outside the indexed corpus, that coverage gap also leads to fp-novel.
prior_verdicts_assessment: The tp verdict is wrong: it claimed promise.spec.ts never exercises `any`, but Promise.spec.ts:661-700 tests it directly. The fp-novel verdict reaches the right kind but argues only from hypothetical application calls, not the actual in-repo test caller.
